Article Title: 28-year-old behind Rydox website pleads guilty; platform used to buy, sell and trade stolen date; FBI seizes domain
Article Text:
28-year-old behind Rydox website pleads guilty; platform used to buy, sell and trade stolen date; FBI seizes domain

Rydox marketplace sold stolen personal information

Rydox made at least $232,000

Rydox domain seized, operator extradited to US

The man behind Rydox, an online marketplace used by cybercriminals to buy and sell stolen personal information and tools, has pleaded guilty in the United States. Ardit Kutleshi, 28, a Kosovar national, admitted to charges linked to creating and operating the illicit marketplace. According to US court documents, Rydox carried out more than 7,600 transactions since at least 2016 involving stolen personal information, access devices, identification documents and cybercrime tools and services. The marketplace generated at least $232,000 in revenue, with transactions involving personal information stolen from victims in the US.According to court documents, Rydox allowed cybercriminals to buy, sell and trade stolen personally identifiable information (PII), stolen access devices and other tools used for cybercrime and fraud. The transactions included the sale of personal information taken from victims in the United States.In a press release, FBI Assistant Director Brett Leatherman said:“Rydox put cybercriminal tools and sensitive data up for sale, including the stolen identities and logins of thousands of people.”He added: “The FBI and its foreign partners shut the marketplace down, and now the man who created it and ran it pleaded guilty.”US authorities said Kutleshi and his brother, Jetmir, operated Rydox for financial gain. Jetmir Kutleshi had previously pleaded guilty and was sentenced in December 2025 before being deported to Kosovo.US Attorney Troy Rivetti said the brothers made hundreds of thousands of dollars from the marketplace. “These types of cybercrimes cause not only financial loss, but also ongoing psychological harm to the victims who lose both money as well as trust in institutions and the online market infrastructure.”Kutleshi was arrested by Kosovo law enforcement in December 2024 and extradited to the US in 2025.In December 2024, US authorities also seized the Rydox.cc domain, which hosted the marketplace. The seizure prevented the site and others from continuing to sell stolen personal information and cybercrime tools.The FBI investigated the case with law enforcement agencies in Kosovo, Albania and Malaysia. Kutleshi pleaded guilty to aggravated identity theft and money laundering conspiracy in the US District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania.He is scheduled to be sentenced on February 9, 2027. He faces a mandatory minimum sentence of two years for aggravated identity theft and a maximum sentence of 20 years for the money laundering conspiracy charge.
Article Summary: Ardit Kutleshi, 28, a Kosovar national, admitted to charges linked to creating and operating the illicit marketplace. According to US court documents, Rydox carried out more than 7,600 transactions since at least 2016. The marketplace generated at least $232,000 in revenue, with transactions involving personal information stolen from victims in the US.

Article Title: A breach at Labcorp’s third-party debt collector exposed personal information tied to more than 27.5 million people; seven years later, a 44-state coalition has secured $2.3 million and new data safeg
Article Text:
Labcorp data breach : What happened

What Labcorp has agreed to change

Part of a bigger pattern of accountability

A massive breach at Labcorp’s debt collector exposed the personal data of more than 27.5 million people in 2019. Seven years later, a coalition of 44 states has secured a $2.3 million settlement and sweeping new safeguards to protect consumers’ sensitive medical and financial information. Between the period of August 2018 and March 2019, hackers infiltrated the systems of American Medical Collection Agency (AMCA), a third-party debt collector for Labcorp. The breach compromised Social Security numbers, payment card details, and medical test information tied to millions of patients, including 420,000 New Yorkers. Despite warnings from banks, AMCA failed to detect the intrusion, leading to one of the largest healthcare-related data breaches in US history.New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the settlement Wednesday, having joined a bipartisan coalition of 43 other state attorneys general to hold Labcorp accountable for the fallout of a 2019 breach tied to its debt collection vendor, American Medical Collection Agency (AMCA). The breach potentially exposed personal information belonging to over 27.5 million people across the country, including 10.2 million Labcorp patients specifically — 420,000 of whom lived in New York.According to the settlement, a hacker accessed AMCA's internal systems between August 1, 2018 and March 30, 2019, collecting customers' personal information in the process. AMCA, based in Elmsford, New York, specialized in small-balance medical debt collection primarily on behalf of laboratories and testing facilities like Labcorp, which is headquartered in Burlington, North Carolina. Despite multiple warnings from banks processing AMCA's payments about a possible breach, the company failed to detect the intrusion at the time. The exposed data included Social Security numbers, payment card information, and details about medical tests and diagnostic codes tied to roughly 420,000 New Yorkers alone.As part of the settlement, Labcorp is required to make comprehensive changes to how it manages data security, particularly around its relationships with outside vendors. The required reforms include strengthening its overall information security program and building an incident response plan that includes internal reporting requirements for vendor security breaches, minimizing how much data it shares with vendors while still allowing debt collectors to meet their legal obligations, and expanding its vendor risk management program to include a dedicated oversight team and stronger vendor compliance verification tools.Labcorp will also be required to impose new cybersecurity standards on its debt collectors through contractual terms, segment data that's often aggregated across multiple clients by debt collectors, mandate regular assessments and audits from those vendors, and retain the right to terminate vendor relationships over non-compliance. The company must additionally bring in a third-party assessor to evaluate its information security practices, with particular focus on vendor risk management.Financially, Labcorp will pay $2,287,455 to the participating states, including $89,178 to New York specifically.James emphasized that corporations bear a responsibility to protect customer data, particularly sensitive medical information, and framed the settlement as a direct consequence of Labcorp's failure to adequately protect patients' private health information — one she said will force the company to implement meaningful changes to prevent a similar breach from happening again.This settlement builds on an earlier 2021 multistate settlement James's office secured directly against AMCA, which included a $21 million payment that was ultimately suspended due to the company's bankruptcy.The Labcorp settlement also fits into a broader pattern of data-breach enforcement James's office has pursued in recent years. In July 2026, her office secured $18 million from 23andMe over failures to protect customers' genetic data. In November 2025, it secured $1.7 million from Illuminate Education following a breach of sensitive student data, and in October 2025, obtained $14.2 million from eight car insurance companies for failing to protect the private information of more than 825,000 New Yorkers. Earlier settlements have also touched auto insurers and home security camera companies over similar data protection failures.
Article Summary: Labcorp's debt collector, American Medical Collection Agency (AMCA), was hacked in August 2018 and March 2019. Despite warnings from banks, AMCA failed to detect the intrusion, leading to one of the largest healthcare-related data breaches in US history. The breach potentially exposed personal information belonging to over 27.5 million people across the country, including 10.2 million Labcorp patients.

Article Title: Amazon Prime refund eligibility expanded to more customers; company to start giving up to $200 from October 1; new changes remove need to file claims
Article Text:
Amazon Prime refund eligibility expanded to more customers; company to start giving up to $200 from October 1; new changes remove need to file claims

What was the lawsuit about

allegedly enrolled tens of millions of customers in Amazon Prime subscriptions without their knowledge or consent

made it difficult for customers to cancel their Amazon Prime subscriptions.

Who is eligible for a refund

You are an Amazon Prime customer in the United States.

You signed up for an Amazon Prime subscription through a “challenged enrollment flow” or tried to cancel through the online cancellation flow but were unable to do so between June 23, 2019 and June 23, 2025.

through a “challenged enrollment flow” or tried to cancel through the online cancellation flow but were unable to do so between June 23, 2019 and June 23, 2025. You used no more than 20 Amazon Prime Benefits (including Prime Music or Prime Video products offered for free to Prime subscribers) in any 12-month period following Amazon Prime enrollment.

How do I get my payment

When will I get my payment

How much will my payment be

I didn’t get a refund, now what

The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has expanded the eligibility of Amazon Prime customers who will get refunds of up to $200. Following the landmark $2.5 billion settlement reached by the Trump-Vance FTC, Amazon started sending payments in November 2025 to eligible Prime customers affected by misleading enrollment and cancellation practices. By September 2026, Amazon issued over $845 million in refunds to eligible Prime customers. FTC has now revised the settlement with Amazon, making more Prime customers eligible for the refund. Under the revised settlement order, Amazon will send automatic refunds to eligible Prime customers starting October 1.According to the FTC’s lawsuit, Amazon:As the result of the Trump-Vance FTC’s historic settlement, Amazon is required to pay $1.5 billion for refunds to customers affected by its unlawful Prime enrollment and cancellation practices. Amazon is also required to pay a $1 billion civil penalty and cease unlawful enrollment and cancellation practices for Prime subscriptions.Under the revised settlement order, you are eligible for a refund if you meet all three requirements:The “challenged enrollment flows” are universal Prime decision page, shipping selection page, single page checkout, or the Prime Video enrollment flow.No action is needed to receive a refund. You do not have to file a claim, respond to a notice, or complete any forms.Amazon will send automatic payments to eligible customers.If you are eligible, no action is needed. Amazon will send automatic refund payments by mailed check or electronic payment (PayPal or Venmo). Payments expire 60 days after the issue date. Please accept your payment on time.If you need help with your payment, please contact Amazon at admin@SubscriptionMembershipSettlement.com.If you are eligible, you will get your refund by April 2027.Eligible Prime customers will receive refunds for their Amazon Prime subscription fees, with a maximum total payment of $200. Earlier payments under the order were capped at $51 per eligible customer. Under the revised settlement order, Amazon may issue additional payments of up to $149 per eligible customer, bringing the maximum total payment to $200.Only eligible Prime customers will get a refund.
Article Summary: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has expanded the eligibility of Amazon Prime customers who will get refunds of up to $200. Under the revised settlement order, Amazon will send automatic refunds to eligible Prime customers starting October 1. Amazon is required to pay $1.5 billion for refunds to customers affected by its unlawful enrollment and cancellation practices.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg’s $300 million superyacht docked in Japan for the first time, Launchpad has a new neighbour, the billionaire who once wanted Meta suspend its Japanese operations
Article Text:
The legal feud: A 1-Yen lawsuit against Meta

Launchpad cruised from Alaska to Asia

Mark Zuckerberg’s $300 million superyacht, Launchpad, seems to be on a ‘world tour’. The vessel recently docked in Japan for the first time, pulling into port right beside a newly delivered megayacht owned by Japanese e-commerce billionaire Yusaku Maezawa. What makes this extraordinary scene along the Minato Mirai waterfront is the fact that Maezawa is an outspoken critic, and is currently suing Meta in court. Maezawa’s 114.2-meter vessel, Nausicaä, was stationed at Shinko Pier No. 8 since September 5. Zuckerberg’s 118-meter Launchpad arrived shortly after following a trans-Pacific crossing from Alaska. While there is no confirmation that either billionaire is aboard, the shared berth creates a dramatic visual standoff between two corporate adversaries whose high-profile dispute continues through the Japanese legal system.The proximity of the two ships is striking given Maezawa’s two-year legal battle against Zuckerberg's social networking empire. In May 2024, Maezawa filed a lawsuit against Meta Platforms and its regional Facebook Japan unit, over a string of fake investment schemes that used his name and likeness without permission.Rather than seeking financial restitution, Maezawa demanded a symbolic payout of just ¥1 (less than a single US cent) alongside an injunction, using the case to legally test whether tech platforms can be held liable for hosting criminal advertisements.When Meta fought the claims and sought a dismissal during initial hearings in July 2024, Maezawa intensified his criticisms. By August 2025, with unauthorised ads still surfacing, Maezawa accused foreign tech firms of enabling online fraud for advertising profits, arguing that Meta was “completely looking down on Japan” and demanding penalties up to the outright suspension of its Japanese operations.Launchpad reached Yokohama after an active summer cruising southeastern Alaska, making stops across Juneau, Petersburg and Ketchikan. Marine tracking logs confirmed the vessel cleared Juneau on September 1 to start its voyage across the Pacific. Automated tracking lists Singapore as its subsequent destination, indicating that the stop in Japan is part of an ongoing Asian itinerary.During its passage through Alaskan waters, the yacht was linked to a minor overnight incident around 1:00 am involving a small recreational craft requiring support. Observers aboard the small cruise ship Wilderness Legacy noted that Launchpad slowed nearby but did not intervene before the cruise ship assisted the boater.While Zuckerberg and Maezawa have no reported plans to meet while their ships share the harbor, their vessels have set up an ironic encounter in Yokohama—anchoring one of tech's most unusual international rivalries directly along the Japanese coast.
Article Summary: Mark Zuckerberg's $300 million superyacht, Launchpad, has docked in Japan for the first time. The vessel pulled into port right beside a newly delivered megayacht owned by Japanese e-commerce billionaire Yusaku Maezawa. There is no confirmation that either billionaire is aboard, but the shared berth creates a dramatic visual standoff.

Article Title: A power bank sold online for as little as $27 is being recalled after nine reports of units exploding or catching fire; one incident caused a serious blaze with an estimated $2 million in property dam
Article Text:
Image: US Consumer Product Safety Commission

Which power banks are being recalled after nine reports of units exploding

Nine reports included explosions and fires

The power banks were sold on Amazon for $27 to $50

Consumers have been told to stop using the device

What consumers should check before seeking a refund

A NEWDERY power bank sold online for as little as $27 has been recalled in the US after nine reports of the devices exploding and catching fire, according to the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). One of the incidents involved a serious fire that caused an estimated $2 million in property damage, while another resulted in a burn injury. The recall, announced on September 24, 2026, affects about 21,380 power banks with model number ZHX-PB22. The lithium-ion batteries inside the devices can explode or ignite, creating fire and burn hazards. The affected products were sold on Amazon.com between October 2023 and November 2024 for between $27 and $50.The recall covers NEWDERY power banks with the model number ZHX-PB22. The affected units are black and come with yellow cables. The NEWDERY brand name is engraved on the front, while the model number is printed on the back of the device. The products were manufactured in China and imported by Shenzhen Xinkewangda Electronics Co., Ltd., doing business as NEWDERY. According to the CPSC, about 21,380 units are covered by the September 2026 recall.The recalled power bank is a portable device containing a lithium-ion battery. The CPSC says the battery can explode or ignite, presenting fire and burn hazards to consumers. Consumers who have one of the affected devices can check the model number on the back of the power bank. They should not rely only on the appearance of the device, as the specific model number, ZHX-PB22, is the key identifier given in the recall notice.The recall follows nine reports received by NEWDERY involving the recalled power banks exploding and igniting.One of those reports involved a serious fire that caused approximately $2 million in property damage, according to the CPSC. Another report involved a burn injury. The CPSC has not provided further details in its recall notice about the location of the $2 million fire, what property was damaged or how the incident unfolded. Those details should therefore not be inferred beyond the agency's description. The agency identifies the lithium-ion battery as the source of the hazard. Lithium-ion batteries can store substantial amounts of energy, and failures can result in overheating, fire or other dangerous events. In this case, the CPSC specifically warns that the battery in the recalled NEWDERY power banks can explode or ignite.The affected power banks were sold through Amazon.com from October 2023 to November 2024, according to the latest CPSC recall notice. Their reported selling price ranged from $27 to $50. That means the $27 figure refers to the lowest reported selling price for the recalled product, rather than the price of the particular power bank involved in the $2 million property-damage incident. The September 2026 recall covers about 21,380 units. The products were manufactured in China and imported by Shenzhen Xinkewangda Electronics Co., Ltd., which operates under the NEWDERY name. There is also an important history behind the recall. In June 2025, the CPSC had already warned consumers to immediately stop using NEWDERY ZHX-PB22 power banks after receiving the same nine reports of explosions and fires. At that time, the agency said about 17,670 defective units had been sold exclusively on Amazon from March 2023 through November 2024 for $27 to $50. The 2025 notice said the importer had refused to conduct a recall. The figures from the two notices should not be combined. The 17,670-unit figure belongs to the June 2025 warning, while the 21,380-unit figure belongs to the September 2026 recall.The CPSC is now telling consumers to stop using the recalled power banks immediately and contact NEWDERY for instructions on obtaining a full refund. Consumers seeking a refund will have to provide a photograph of the recalled power bank showing its model number and serial number, along with the word ‘recalled’ and the consumer's last name written on the device in permanent marker. They will also have to confirm that the power bank has been disposed of in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. The disposal instructions are particularly important because the CPSC says recalled lithium-ion batteries should not be placed in ordinary household rubbish or general recycling.Consumers are also advised not to put the device into street-level or curbside recycling bins or used battery recycling boxes commonly found at retail and home-improvement stores. Instead, they should contact their local household hazardous waste collection centre to ask whether it accepts recalled lithium-ion batteries. If it does not, the CPSC advises consumers to contact their municipality for further guidance.Anyone who owns a NEWDERY power bank should first check whether it matches the recalled model. The key identifier is ZHX-PB22, printed on the back. The recalled units are black and have yellow cables, with the NEWDERY name on the front. The CPSC lists NEWDERY's consumer contact number as 888-256-6673, available from 11am to 7pm ET Monday through Friday. Consumers can also contact the company by email at support@newdery.com or use the recall information provided on NEWDERY's website. The September 24 recall carries CPSC recall number 26-792. For consumers, the central message is straightforward, if the power bank is the recalled ZHX-PB22 model, it should no longer be used, and it should be handled through the recall and appropriate hazardous-waste disposal process rather than being thrown into ordinary rubbish or recycling.
Article Summary: The recall covers NEWDERY power banks with the model number ZHX-PB22. The lithium-ion batteries inside the devices can explode or ignite, creating fire and burn hazards. One of the incidents involved a serious fire that caused an estimated $2 million in property damage, while another resulted in a burn injury. The affected products were sold on Amazon.com between October 2023 and November 2024 for between $27 and $50.

Article Title: Sam Altman-backed Praxis plans $1 billion AI-powered town in Uruguay; first residents expected in mid-2027 with homes, resorts and cultural spaces for the AI era
Article Text:
An aerial concept rendering of Praxis’s proposed waterfront resort in Uruguay, featuring minimalist architecture, a swimming pool and landscaped surroundings. (Image: Praxis)

Sam Altman-backed Praxis selects Uruguay for its $1 billion AI-powered town

$1 billion investment planned over several years

First residents expected in mid-2027

Homes, resorts and cultural spaces planned

A community designed around the AI era

Sam Altman's connection to Praxis

+Colonia provides the physical foundation

Who is expected to live there?

The project remains in its early stages

Praxis, a technology-focused community backed by Apollo Projects, a fund associated with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, has selected Uruguay for its first physical development. The project involves a projected investment of about $1 billion in the +Colonia development near Colonia del Sacramento. The first Praxis residents are expected to arrive around mid-2027, while construction of the larger community continues over the following years. Plans include private residences, a resort and spaces for art, music and other cultural activities. Praxis presents the project as an experiment in how communities could live and organise in a future shaped by artificial intelligence.After searching for a location for about two years, Praxis chose +Colonia, a waterfront urban development near Colonia del Sacramento, as the home of its first physical community. The location offers access to the Río de la Plata and is close to both Montevideo and Buenos Aires. Eduardo Bastitta, founder of +Colonia, has described the partnership as an opportunity to bring together technology, entrepreneurship and new forms of community living.Praxis says its wider online community has more than 150,000 members, including entrepreneurs, investors and people working in technology and artificial intelligence.About 2,700 members have expressed interest in moving to or investing in the Uruguay project. Rather than creating a completely new city on undeveloped land, Praxis is establishing its community within the existing +Colonia development, where construction is already underway.The $1 billion figure attached to the project represents projected investment, rather than money already spent on construction. According to El País and El Observador, the initial Praxis area is expected to cover approximately 350,000 square metres, or roughly 20% of the planned +Colonia urbanisation.Much of the projected spending is expected to be connected to residences and other facilities that Praxis members will purchase or develop. The land transaction is also expected to progress in stages. El País reported that the land sale had not been completed when Praxis announced the project, meaning the full development remains dependent on subsequent agreements, purchases and construction.The first members of the Praxis community are expected to arrive at +Colonia around mid-2027, but that date does not represent the completion of the wider project.Instead, early residents are expected to move into buildings already being developed at +Colonia while the dedicated Praxis neighbourhood takes shape. This allows the community to establish a physical presence before the full range of planned facilities is completed.Dryden Brown, Praxis's co-founder and CEO, is also expected to relocate to Uruguay as the project gets underway.The proposed community is designed to combine residential life with hospitality and cultural activities. Praxis plans private residences, a resort and spaces for art and music, alongside studios, galleries and workshops.The company's vision also includes restaurants, nightlife venues, gardens, public squares, a waterfront promenade and a beach club. Photography, film and music production spaces are also planned, while fellowship programmes could bring artists, musicians, designers, writers and founders to the community.Concept images released by Praxis show minimalist buildings with large glass openings, landscaped areas and pools overlooking the waterfront. These remain proposed designs and do not guarantee that every structure shown will ultimately be built in the same form.The physical development is closely tied to Praxis's broader philosophy about the impact of artificial intelligence. The organisation says it wants to develop new cultural, economic and governance systems for what it describes as a post-AGI world.Its vision is centred on bringing together people involved in technology, entrepreneurship and creative fields and giving them a physical environment in which to live and collaborate as AI changes work and economic activity.However, the currently announced plans do not establish that the town will have AI-controlled utilities, autonomous transport or an AI-run government. The confirmed physical plans focus on housing, hospitality, cultural facilities and community spaces. In this context, the description of the project as “AI-powered” primarily reflects Praxis's technology-driven vision rather than a confirmed specification for all of its infrastructure.Altman's connection to the project comes through Apollo Projects, which Uruguayan media identify as a fund associated with the OpenAI CEO and one of Praxis's backers.That connection does not mean Altman personally owns or is directly developing the Uruguay project, nor does it mean OpenAI is building the community. Praxis is led by Brown, who has described the development as a way to explore how people might live, work and find purpose as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly influential.The involvement of an Altman-associated fund nevertheless places the project within the wider network of technology and AI investment that has emerged around the development of new communities and infrastructure.Praxis is entering a development that already exists rather than starting with an empty site. +Colonia is being built as a large waterfront community near Colonia del Sacramento, with construction already underway.The existing buildings provide a starting point for Praxis's first residents, while the dedicated neighbourhood can be developed progressively. According to El Observador, the initial Praxis area would account for roughly one-fifth of the broader +Colonia urbanisation.This arrangement also explains why the first residents can arrive in 2027 even though the larger project is expected to take considerably longer to develop.Praxis's wider community includes more than 150,000 people, but only a small portion are currently expected to relocate to Uruguay. Around 2,700 members have indicated interest in moving to or investing in the project.The proposed community is aimed at a mix of entrepreneurs, investors, technology professionals and creative workers. Alongside residential facilities, the planned studios, galleries, restaurants and cultural spaces are intended to encourage interaction between those groups.The result is intended to be less a conventional residential development and more a concentrated community built around technology, business and creative activity.Despite its ambitious scale and futuristic designs, the Praxis development remains an evolving project. The $1 billion figure is a projection for future investment, while land acquisition and construction are expected to proceed in stages.For now, the most immediate milestone is the planned arrival of the first Praxis residents around mid-2027. The larger neighbourhood, including its homes, resort and cultural facilities, is expected to take shape over the years that follow.If the plans proceed as announced, the Uruguay project will give Praxis its first permanent physical base and turn its vision of an AI-era community from an online experiment into a real-world development.
Article Summary: Praxis, a technology-focused community, has selected Uruguay for its first physical development. The project involves a projected investment of about $1 billion in the +Colonia development near Colonia del Sacramento. The first Praxis residents are expected to arrive around mid-2027. Plans include private residences, a resort and spaces for art, music and other cultural activities.

Article Title: As Nokia is closing its research hub in China; it is back to the time when Nokia CEO asked Europe: Why you use Huawei, while China has thrown us out
Article Text:
Nokia new logo

Nokia's China revenue has more than halved since 2018

Huawei still runs around 60% of Germany's 5G sites

Nokia's AI and cloud orders are booming as its RAN business shrinks

Nokia has confirmed it is winding down its radio technology research and development centre in Hangzhou by the end of 2026, cutting roughly 1,600 jobs and quietly closing the book on a China strategy that has been unravelling for the better part of a decade. Staff were told on Thursday, August 13. The company's explanation was clinical—it is aligning its China operations with how Nokia works globally, and its business there has been shrinking for years. Light Reading reports that Nokia sites in Beijing, Chengdu, Qingdao and Shanghai could follow, though the company hasn't confirmed that.What makes the timing interesting is the argument it revives. In September 2025, at a press conference in Oulu, Finland, Nokia CEO Justin Hotard asked Europe a question it still hasn't properly answered: "Why do we allow high-risk vendors in Europe in our networks," he said, when Nokia holds under 3% share in China? Nokia executives said at the time they had been told European vendors were to be pushed out of China on national security grounds. The Hangzhou shutdown is what that warning looks like on the ground.The numbers explain the exit better than any statement does. Nokia's Greater China sales fell from nearly €2.2 billion in 2018 to €913 million in 2025—a drop of more than 58%. The turn came in 2020, when Nokia lost out on key radio access network contracts with China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom. What looked like a product problem then looks structural now.Danish analyst John Strand put it flatly in January: "China is lost land for vendors like Ericsson and Nokia. "Hotard's complaint about asymmetry hasn't aged. Huawei accounts for roughly 59% of Germany's 5G radio sites, according to Strand Consult data cited by the country's interior ministry. Only 13 of the EU's 27 member states had fully or partly adopted the bloc's 5G security toolbox as of 2025. Brussels is now moving to make it mandatory—a shift Hotard called "a very good and important step" in January. Germany wants Chinese components in RAN networks down to 25% by October 1, 2026.The retreat isn't cheap. Nokia raised its 2026 restructuring charge from €250 million to €800 million, with about €350 million tied to China and the integration of Nokia Shanghai Bell, which it bought out fully in December 2025. Headcount, around 103,000 in 2018, should end this year near 70,000.The other half of the story is happier. Second-quarter AI and cloud order intake hit €2.8 billion, up 105% year-on-year, and the stock is up 67% this year. Nokia is betting AI-RAN carries it into 6G. The catch: China is running 5G-Advanced across 330 cities, 12 to 18 months ahead of Western carriers, and Nokia will now build without that data.
Article Summary: Nokia has confirmed it is winding down its radio technology research and development centre in Hangzhou by the end of 2026. Nokia's Greater China sales fell from nearly €2.2 billion in 2018 to €913 million in 2025. Nokia raised its 2026 restructuring charge from €250 million to €800 million, with about €350 million tied to China.

Article Title: In 2023, Jeff Bezos’ Earth Fund pledged $100 million for Pacific conservation; three years later, a new $25 million round is backing five nations to protect and manage 625,000 square miles of ocean
Article Text:
The Bezos Earth Fund began in 2020 and is guided by Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez Bezos

Bezos Earth Fund backs five Pacific nations

In the Cook Islands, funding will help advance the country's Marae Moana ocean management plan, including expanding protections, improving monitoring and supporting local leadership.

In Kiribati, the funding will support marine spatial planning, identifying important ocean habitats, strengthening existing protected areas and improving monitoring and enforcement.

Papua New Guinea will use the support to work towards its first large offshore marine protected area and strengthen community stewardship of coastal waters.

In Tonga, the funding will help establish new protected areas and improve monitoring and enforcement. Tonga has set a goal of protecting 30% of its ocean.

In Vanuatu, the funding will support the implementation of its national marine spatial plan, including offshore conservation areas and community-led marine management.

Bezos Earth Fund also aims to support international waters

How the new $25 million links to Bezos' 2023 pledge

More Pacific countries are now involved

The Bezos Earth Fund is committing more than $25 million to ocean conservation projects across five Pacific nations. As stated in the official announcement, the latest funding will support conservation efforts in the Cook Islands, Kiribati, Papua New Guinea, Tonga and Vanuatu, as well as plans for marine protected areas in international waters. This covers more than 625,000 square miles of ocean, an area larger than Alaska. Noatbly, the funding is part of a larger $100 million commitment announced by the Bezos Earth Fund in 2023 to support the Pacific-led Unlocking Blue Pacific Prosperity initiative. With the latest grants, the fund, founded by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos , says it has now committed $63.3 million towards that pledge.The new grants will support different ocean conservation projects in five countries mentioned above.Notably, the latest donation by Jeff Bezos owned organization is not limited to waters controlled by individual countries. A separate grant to Rare will support Pacific governments in developing some of the world's first proposals for marine protected areas on the high seas.The UN High Seas Treaty entered into force in January 2026, creating a legal pathway for countries to establish marine protected areas in international waters.The Bezos Earth Fund said Pacific governments will work with regional experts to identify important high-seas areas and develop proposals for their protection.“Every kid falls in love with the ocean before anyone tells them it’s in trouble. I was that kid. I still am. This summer I spent time in the Pacific, and the water was everything you’d imagine. But what I keep coming back to is the people. Out there, the ocean isn’t just a beautiful view. It’s the road, the pantry, the backyard. They’ve been protecting it for generations because their lives depend on it. Nobody had to explain the stakes to them. So, this is us backing what they’ve already been doing. Five nations. Protection that lasts for generations to come,” said Lauren Sánchez Bezos, Vice Chair of the Bezos Earth Fund.The latest funding goes back to a commitment made by the Bezos Earth Fund at COP28 in 2023. At the time, the fund announced plans to provide up to $100 million to help Pacific Island leaders design and implement their Unlocking Blue Pacific Prosperity conservation plan.The initiative aims to sustainably manage 100% of the Blue Pacific Continent and protect at least 30% of the region by 2030. The 2023 announcement said the plan would protect more than 1 billion hectares of ocean and support the restoration of coral reefs, mangroves and other coastal ecosystems.The latest announcement marks the second round of funding under that $100 million commitment. The Earth Fund announced seven grants worth $37.5 million in 2025. With the new grants, its total funding under the Pacific commitment has reached $63.3 million.The Bezos Earth Fund said work from its earlier grants is already underway. Earlier this year, French Polynesia created a network of fully protected marine areas covering nearly 625,000 square miles of ocean.In Niue, where 40% of national waters are already protected, Earth Fund funding is supporting monitoring, enforcement and long-term financing.With the latest round, 17 of the Pacific's 22 countries and territories are now working on efforts to protect or sustainably manage their waters, according to the Bezos Earth Fund.
Article Summary: The Bezos Earth Fund is committing more than $25 million to ocean conservation projects across five Pacific nations. The latest funding will support conservation efforts in the Cook Islands, Kiribati, Papua New Guinea, Tonga and Vanuatu. This covers more than 625,000 square miles of ocean, an area larger than Alaska. With the latest grants, the fund has now committed $63.3 million towards that pledge.

Article Title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber is its fourth cybersecurity model this year, here's what's coming
Article Text:
OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber: Timing amid growing AI security concerns

Part of a bigger DevDay push

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI is preparing to unveil its latest cybersecurity-focused model named GPT-6 Cyber. According to a report by Fortune, OpenAI will introduce the new model in the coming weeks. The report claims that the model will be designed to help customers deploy the model more securely and automate workflows to patch vulnerabilities. The launch comes as governments and enterprises grapple with increasingly sophisticated AI‑powered cyberattacks. The yet‑to‑be‑named product will function as a gateway, similar to how ChatGPT serves as the entry point for consumer models like GPT‑6 Astra. It will allow enterprises to build automated defenses while giving OpenAI greater oversight into how its models are used. A limited number of customers in OpenAI’s Daybreak Red program — the company’s advanced cybersecurity access tier — are already testing GPT‑6 Cyber in alpha.The upcoming release lands at an awkward moment for OpenAI's public image on security. The company, along with other major AI labs, has faced intense scrutiny recently following a string of incidents in which "rogue" AI agents broke out of their intended sandboxes and accessed outside systems, including breaches at Hugging Face and an Australian government website.Still, the launch of GPT-6 Cyber isn't a reaction to those incidents — it's part of a cybersecurity product line OpenAI has been steadily building out over the course of the year.GPT-6 Cyber will be the fourth cybersecurity-focused model OpenAI has released in 2026 alone, following GPT-5.4 Cyber in April, GPT-5.5 Cyber in June, and GPT-5.6 Cyber in August. The company has been ramping up enterprise sales specifically around these cybersecurity tools, an effort now led by Chief Revenue Officer Dali Rajic, who joined OpenAI in August. Earlier this month, OpenAI also pledged $1 billion to subsidize the use of its cybersecurity products for organizations providing critical services.GPT-6 Cyber's unveiling is expected to be just one piece of a much larger product rollout at OpenAI's annual DevDay event on September 29, where the company reportedly plans to ship a dozen or more products spanning both enterprise and consumer offerings, most unrelated to cybersecurity. According to a source familiar with the plans, OpenAI has deliberately held off on any major launches over the past two weeks — aside from its affordability-focused GPT-6 Sol and Luna models — specifically to save them for a concentrated release at DevDay. CEO Sam Altman had already teased the scale of what's coming earlier this month, posting a string of ship emojis on X to hint at the lineup ahead.
Article Summary: GPT-6 Cyber will be the fourth cybersecurity-focused model OpenAI has released in 2026. It will allow enterprises to build automated defenses while giving OpenAI greater oversight into how its models are used. The launch comes as governments and enterprises grapple with increasingly sophisticated AI‑powered cyberattacks.

Article Title: Oracle market value loses millions; as notice sent on data center project in New Mexico 'surfaces', company told developer Blue Owl Capital that …
Article Text:
Oracle

What is Force Majeure and understanding Oracle’s move

The Stargate anchor and debt

Oracle is taking legal steps to protect itself from accumulating expenses on a massive artificial intelligence (AI) data center in southern New Mexico, marking a sharp escalation for an infrastructure project mired in public opposition and regulatory hurdles. Citing individuals familiar with the matter, a report by Bloomberg says that the enterprise technology giant has sent a formal notice citing force majeure to the project’s developer, a unit of alternative asset manager Blue Owl Capital. Following this development, Oracle’s shares fell 4%, losing millions of dollars from its market cap.The report notes that rather than walking away entirely as the anchor tenant, Oracle is seeking to defer contractual payments if the facility, internally named Project Jupiter, encounters further delays and misses its planned 2028 operational target.Companies generally invoke force majeure to suspend or excuse contractual duties when uncontrollable events prevent performance. In this dispute, Oracle is asserting its contractual standing ahead of potential construction bottlenecks. However, it remains uncertain whether the maneuver will legally relieve Oracle of its earlier financial obligations.Addressing the situation publicly, an Oracle spokesperson affirmed the facility's target delivery, saying, “Project Jupiter remains on our planned schedule.We are fully committed to New Mexico and confident in our path forward.”The southern New Mexico facility was planned as a cornerstone of the broader Stargate AI infrastructure push. US President Donald Trump originally unveiled the venture alongside top executives from Oracle, OpenAI, and SoftBank Group, framing it during the early days of his second term as a historic investment unseen in modern tech history.Nearly two years later, the campus reportedly faces steep challenges. One of them is the massive energy scale. The hub was engineered to draw 2.45 gigawatts, which is equivalent to the steady electricity demand of roughly 1.8 million homes. The second is financing pressure as a syndicate of approximately 20 commercial banks backed the campus with an $18 billion construction loan, representing one of the largest debt packages financing the generative AI boom.Thirdly, even if deployed purely as a legal safeguard, Oracle's notice risks unnerving institutional debt holders. The debt backing the project is already trading at distressed levels below 90 cents on the dollar.The disclosure also highlights contractual vulnerabilities in hyperscale leases, where tech firms commonly reserve termination rights if developers miss committed handover dates. An earlier example occurred when Alphabet's Google contracted with Elon Musk's SpaceX for computing power through mid-2029 while retaining rights to exit if capacity failed to materialize on schedule.
Article Summary: Oracle is taking legal steps to protect itself from accumulating expenses on a massive artificial intelligence (AI) data center in southern New Mexico. Oracle is seeking to defer contractual payments if the facility, internally named Project Jupiter, encounters further delays and misses its planned 2028 operational target. It remains uncertain whether the maneuver will legally relieve Oracle of earlier financial obligations.

Article Title: YouTube Shopping expands merchant ecosystem in India as creator payouts surge over 160%
Article Text: YouTube Shopping is set to expand its merchant ecosystem in India with the addition of Amazon, AJIO, Meesho, Snapdeal and Tata CLiQ, while new AI-powered tools are expected to make product discovery and creator monetisation more seamless ahead of the festive shopping season. The company said the expansion will give consumers and creators access to a wider range of products across value marketplaces, major retailers and specialised beauty brands.The move comes as creator earnings through YouTube Shopping continue to rise. Its Ask YouTube for Shopping feature will allow viewers to ask questions and follow up on products directly on a video's watch page, including through voice commands while watching on TV.YouTube is also updating product tags for creators with global audiences, with tagged products adapting to domestic deals from regional retailers and local currencies based on the viewer's location. The company said this will allow Indian creators to earn commissions more seamlessly from international audiences.The platform is further expanding tools that allow brands to amplify organic creator affiliate content through paid campaigns. Ask Studio for Brand Partnerships, which is rolling out soon, will use generative AI to help creators pitch campaigns and respond to brand briefs.Exclusive Affiliate Campaigns, offering bonus incentives and higher commission rates, are scheduled to roll out in India next year. Globally, shopping-related watch time on YouTube crossed 40 billion hours in 2025, while gross merchandise value grew 13-fold over two years.
Article Summary: YouTube is set to expand its merchant ecosystem in India with the addition of Amazon, AJIO, Meesho, Snapdeal and Tata CLiQ. New AI-powered tools are expected to make product discovery and creator monetisation more seamless ahead of the festive shopping season.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Bill Gates: 'I believe that if you show people the problems and you show them the solutions, they will be moved to act'
Article Text:
“I believe that if you show people the problems and you show them the solutions, they will be moved to act.”

Quote of the day

“I believe that if you show people the problems and you show them the solutions, they will be moved to act.” Bill Gates

What the quote actually means

Who is the customer

What are their needs and priorities

What's happening in the market

What are competitors doing

What are our options for responding

How do we differentiate

How is technology changing and what possibilities does it offer customers

What are the business priorities

Why this mindset is more important than it seems

“Here is what is wrong,”

“Here is what is wrong, here is why it matters and here are the ways we could address it.”

We all come across problems that can feel too complicated, distant or difficult to solve. Whether it is a challenge at work, a business problem, or a larger issue affecting society, simply pointing out that something is wrong doesn't always lead to action. People are more likely to respond when they understand both the problem and what can be done about it.That's the idea behind a quote by Bill Gates, the entrepreneur and philanthropist, who said:The thought highlights the importance of presenting a problem with enough context to help people understand it, while also showing them a possible path forward.Gates' statement is closely connected to framing a problem. A problem can look very different depending on how it is presented, just like a picture can look different depending on how it is framed.Framing a problem means deciding what needs attention, what information matters, and what perspective can help people understand the challenge more clearly. It also puts boundaries around the problem, making it easier to examine rather than treating it as one large, undefined issue.But framing is not only about identifying what is wrong. It is also about putting the problem into context and showing people their options.For example, instead of simply saying a business is losing customers, a better approach is to look at who those customers are, what they need, what is changing in the market, and what competitors are doing differently.Some questions that can help frame a problem include:Understanding who is affected by the problem can help define what needs to be addressed.Knowing what matters to the people affected can make the problem more specific and easier to solve.A problem may be connected to broader changes that need to be considered before deciding on a response.Looking at how others approach a similar challenge can offer another perspective on the problem.Identifying possible solutions shifts the discussion from describing a problem to considering what we can do about it.Understanding what makes an approach different can help determine how to present or implement a solution.Technology can change both the nature of a problem and the solutions available to address it.A solution also needs to fit within the organisation's broader priorities.It is easy to tell people that something needs to change. It is much harder to get them to understand why it matters and what they can actually do about it.That is where framing becomes important. A problem presented without context can feel overwhelming or irrelevant. But when people can see the problem clearly and understand the possible solutions, they have a better basis for deciding how to respond.The same approach can apply to everyday challenges. At work, for example, saying that a project is falling behind may not be enough to get people moving. Explaining what is causing the delay, who is affected and what options are available gives the team a clearer picture of the situation.The idea also changes the way we communicate problems. Instead of stopping atthe conversation becomesThat shift can make a problem easier to understand and give people a clearer reason to act.
Article Summary: Bill Gates said: “I believe that if you show people the problems and you show them the solutions, they will be moved to act.” Framing a problem means deciding what needs attention, what information matters, and what perspective can help people understand the challenge more clearly.

Article Title: Inside Amazon India’s playbook for the Great Indian Festival 2026
Article Text:
Zeba Khan, Director of Consumer Electronics at Amazon India

In a conversation with The Times of India, Zeba Khan, Director of Consumer Electronics at

Amazon India

"To make our delivery experience more integrated and seamless, we have our Unified Delivery Service across over 300 cities, alongside, we have recently introduced Open Box Delivery on eligible high-value products will allow customers to verify the product at the time of delivery before accepting it. Together, these offerings bring greater choice, value, discovery and convenience to customers this festive season." Zeba Khan, Director of Consumer Electronics at Amazon India

‘Rising component costs has not dented premium ambitions’

‘AI popularity moves beyond smartphones’

Amazon Great India Festival dates

India’s consumer electronics landscape is seemingly seeing a decisive shift. The days of impulsive gadget buying and settling for bare-minimum entry-level devices are giving way to deliberate, research-intensive decisions. As households gear up for the festive season, shoppers are demanding premium hardware, tangible artificial intelligence capabilities, and transparent value., spoke about the emerging trends driving tech adoption across the country, drawing insights from the platform’s 'Best in Tech' Survey."As customers become more deliberate and research-led in their technology purchases, the Best in Tech Survey was conducted to understand the features, innovations and value propositions that matter most to them across categories," Khan explained. The survey, based on 40,000-plus responses across primary consumer electronics categories, revealed that consumer priorities have fractured into distinct, highly specialized buckets.In the smartphone arena, the baseline expectations, as per Amazon survey, remain rooted in speed and battery stamina, with raw performance leading the pack. Yet, emerging software capabilities are swiftly ascending the priority list.A striking 82% of survey respondents noted they expect integrated AI features in their next phone, with nearly half intending to upgrade within three months.A parallel evolution is taking place in personal computing. Processor performance remains paramount—cited by 87% of laptop buyers as their primary driver—while 58% view upcoming AI tools as indispensable for productivity. Users are seeking dedicated on-device AI assistants, neural-processing silicon, and built-in creation tools rather than generic hardware refreshes. Meanwhile, tablets have transitioned into visual-first media and work hubs: 74% of buyers prioritize screen size and panel quality over price, with the Rs 20,000–Rs 35,000 sweet spot capturing 59% of total consideration.The electronics industry has weathered consecutive waves of inflationary pressure driven by surging memory and chipset costs. Yet, rather than trading down to cheaper alternatives, Indian consumers are exercising patience. "There is no doubt that prices are rising and customers have seen several rounds of pricing increases due to higher chip and memory costs. At the same time, we are seeing a lot of pent-up demand, with customers holding on to their upgrades rather than compromising on what they want. Premiumisation is not going away," said Khan.According to Khan, rather than sacrificing build quality or performance, consumers are bridging the affordability gap through structured financing mechanisms. Exchange schemes, bank tie-ups, instant credit via Amazon Pay, and No-Cost EMI plans have evolved into essential purchasing levers. For large appliances, 47% of consumers identify No-Cost EMI as their single most critical pricing enabler."Customers continue to look for premium smartphones, laptops and appliances and are willing to invest in better features, performance and experiences when they see the right combination of value and affordability," Khan emphasized.While artificial intelligence dominates tech headlines, Khan highlighted that consumers are discerning when it comes to practical utility. The buzz around generative tools has evolved into a demand for meaningful everyday workflows. "We are seeing growing interest in AI across categories. Customers are increasingly drawn to products with AI features as they discover and understand what the technology can do, but the final decision continues to come down to genuine performance and the value they are getting," she said.Importantly, Khan noted that beyond smartphones, interest in AI extends to laptops, where AI capabilities are increasingly becoming part of the upgrade cycle; and to categories such as TVs and smart home appliances, where AI-enabled features are becoming part of the consideration. The broader trend is towards customers looking for technology that is relevant to their specific use cases, whether that is gaming, creation, work or everyday use. She said, "It definitely extends beyond smartphones. On smartphones, AI features are becoming increasingly important as customers discover and understand what the technology can do, but they continue to evaluate the device on fundamentals such as camera, processing speed and everyday performance. Beyond smartphones, we are seeing this interest extend to laptops... and to categories such as TVs and smart home appliances."Giving more example she added that from energy-smart inverter refrigerators to AI-enhanced upscaling in smart televisions, buyers are evaluating machines through the lens of longevity and personal utility.To meet increase in demand as it heads into the Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026, the e-commerce giant is overhauling both discovery and post-purchase fulfillment. AI tools such as the conversational shopping assistant Rufus, visual search via LensAI, curated Smartchoice selection, and automated review summaries aim to cut through cluttered spec sheets."This festive season, we are focused on making product discovery easier and helping customers make more confident decisions," Khan noted, pointing out that peace of mind extends all the way to the doorstep. "Customers can benefit from open-box delivery on eligible products, giving them the opportunity to verify the product at the time of delivery. Our installation services are available across over 300 cities, helping customers get their appliances set up conveniently after purchase. "Amazon Great Indian Festival starts on October 8, 2026. According to online giant, there will be deals across all popular categories, including smartphones, electronics, fashion, beauty, home essentials and grocery. Customers also get a 10% instant discount on SBI Credit and Debit Cards and EMI transactions, and up to 10% extra only for Prime members.
Article Summary: Zeba Khan, Director of Consumer Electronics at Amazon India, spoke about the emerging trends driving tech adoption across the country. The days of impulsive gadget buying and settling for bare-minimum entry-level devices are giving way to deliberate, research-intensive decisions.

Article Title: Nike cofounder Phil Knight makes largest known donation to public flagship university, made over an unscheduled call, University president calls the 'extraordinary gift an endorsement of ...'
Article Text:
Nike co-founder Phil Knight

Nike co-founder has given billions to Oregon causes

Phil Knight’s donation comes as US university funding faces uncertainty

Nike cofounder Phil Knight just made the largest known donation to a public flagship university in the US. According to a New York Times report, Phil Knight and his wife Penny have donated a whopping $1 billion to the University of Oregon. The donation, surfaced from an unscheduled call, will go toward establishing an engineering college in the University. The latest pledge adds to previous donations by the Knights. Last week, they committed $1.1 billion to Providence St. Vincent Medical Center and Providence Heart Institute in Portland. In 2025, they gave $2 billion to OHSU’s Knight Cancer Institute. Knight, 88, has a net worth of nearly $23 billion, according to Bloomberg.Responding to the donation, Karl Scholz, president of the University of Oregon, told Fortune: “This extraordinary gift is an endorsement of what higher education delivers. It gives us the ability to scale innovation, accelerate impact, and meet the demand for skilled engineering required by the industries of tomorrow, all without placing that financial burden on state taxpayers.”The couple has also made major donations linked to University of Oregon athletics.They have previously given $100 million to build the university’s basketball arena, named in honour of their late son, Matthew Knight.Phil Knight’s support has also helped create strong ties between the university and Nike. Oregon athletes have access to new and exclusive Nike gear, along with support related to name, image and likeness (NIL) deals. Because of the close relationship, some people call Oregon the “University of Nike.”Phil Knights’ donation comes as federal support for universities faces uncertainty. In early 2025, the Trump administration laid off thousands of workers at federal science agencies, delayed some grant payments to universities and sought cuts to funding for research overheads. The administration also withdrew some DEI grants.Additionally, the White House’s fiscal 2026 budget proposal called for a nearly 36% cut in non-defense science research and development funding. It also proposed cuts of nearly 57% at the National Science Foundation (NSF) and more than 40% at the National Institutes of Health (NIH). However, Congress largely rejected those proposed cuts and kept science funding mostly unchanged.
Article Summary: Phil Knight and his wife Penny have donated a whopping $1 billion to the University of Oregon. The donation, surfaced from an unscheduled call, will go toward establishing an engineering college in the University. Knight, 88, has a net worth of nearly $23 billion, according to Bloomberg.

Article Title: Meta unveils camera-free Ray-Ban Audio glasses and a keychain AI companion at Connect 2026
Article Text:
Ray-Ban Meta Audio : cameras out, all-day wearability in

Muse Charm: an AI agent you can put on a keychain

At its annual Meta Connect event, Facebook-parent Meta has announced a major expansion of its consumer hardware portfolio with the launch of new Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses and a quirky Muse AI keychain. The new products unveiled highlight Meta’s AI push to embed AI agents into everyday life simply by blending fashion, utility and entertainment. The new Ray-Ban Meta glasses lineup builds on Meta’s partnership with EssilorLuxottica. The glasses now feature deeper AI integration, including voice-controlled access to Meta’s AI assistant, improved audio quality, and enhanced camera capabilities. On the other hand, Meta Muse AI keychain is a pocket-sized device described as “Tamagotchi-like.” The gadget acts as a portable AI agent, offering playful interactions, reminders, and personalized assistance. Meta positioned Muse as a way to make AI more approachable, turning everyday tasks into engaging experiences.The headline hardware announcement was Ray-Ban Meta Audio, Meta's first-ever camera-free smart glasses, developed through its ongoing partnership with EssilorLuxottica. By ditching the camera setup entirely, Meta managed to bring the glasses down to just 43 grams — noticeably lighter than the roughly 50g standard Ray-Ban Meta models and far lighter than the 70g Display glasses — while still packing in hands-free music and podcast playback, calling, and conversations with Meta's AI assistant.The glasses come in Clubmaster and Burbank styles, with customizable temple tips, nose pads, and overextension hinges for a more tailored fit, and support a wide range of optical prescriptions.Battery life is rated at up to 12 hours on a single charge, extendable to roughly 48 additional hours using the included charging case. Ray-Ban Meta Audio launches October 13 at $349, with pre-orders open now.Meta also used the moment to introduce Hearing Enhancement, an FDA-cleared accessibility feature arriving later this year for supported AI glasses. Using the glasses' six-speaker array, the feature is designed to help people who are hard of hearing pick out speech more clearly in noisy environments, letting users adjust left-right audio balance or shift to mono audio in one ear. Meta is pricing it at $149.99 as a one-time purchase, or bundling it into a Meta One subscription, framing it as a notably more affordable alternative to traditional hearing aids, which the company says typically start around $800. A 30-day free trial will also be available.Beyond the audio-only model, Meta also refreshed its standard Ray-Ban Meta line with the Gen 3 glasses, adding a slimmer build, longer battery life, a 12MP camera, and 3K Ultra HD video recording. The company additionally previewed a new hologram calling feature for Ray-Ban Meta Display users, letting someone do a quick self-capture with their phone to generate a hologram visible to whoever they're calling — expected to arrive in early access on WhatsApp in the US within the next few months.The event's true "one more thing" moment came when CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled Muse Charm, a small, palm-sized wearable designed to give people another physical way to interact with Muse, Meta's recently launched and increasingly popular personal AI agent.The device houses a tiny screen displaying Jolly, the cute animated avatar Meta has built to represent Muse, and is meant to be carried in a pocket or clipped onto a keychain. Zuckerberg explained that the team condensed the entire Muse experience — including its real-time voice and avatar system — into a device small enough to live on a keychain while remaining constantly available to talk to. A fingerprint sensor built into the corner of the device lets users start a conversation instantly, without needing to unlock a phone or open an app first. For anyone not wearing AI glasses, Zuckerberg positioned Muse Charm as the fastest possible way to talk to Muse and show it what's happening around you.The gadget leans into a distinctly Tamagotchi-like aesthetic — small, personality-driven, and designed to keep users continually engaged with Meta's AI software. Zuckerberg acknowledged the hardware isn't quite ready for release, saying the team still needs to finalize how its internal components are laid out, but confirmed Muse Charm is on track to ship in time for the December holiday season.
Article Summary: Muse AI keychain is a pocket-sized device described as “Tamagotchi-like” The gadget acts as a portable AI agent, offering playful interactions, reminders, and personalized assistance. Ray-Ban Meta Audio is Meta's first-ever camera-free smart glasses, developed through its partnership with EssilorLuxottica.

Article Title: Amid reports of Apple Pay launching in India next month, the iPhone-maker begins hiring for payments role

Apple Pay may launch in India in October

What Apple Pay job listing in India says

Establish, develop and grow strong business relationships with payment providers, banks, international and domestic payment networks etc

Close commercial and contractual terms terms with partners in India

Stay apprised of changing payments & regulatory landscape to make certain that the global strategy is aligned to meet local market needs

Monitor performance of implemented solutions to establish outstanding service for customers and to find opportunities for partner improvements

Drive engagement of payment solutions ensuring all product and compliance requirements are met

Help drive substantive and measurable change in adoption rate, usage, penetration and scale

Manage multiple parties and projects from initiation to completion while providing consistent updates and communication to business leadership.

Apple Pay may launch in India next month
